config.title: Status Card

intro.title: Status Card
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Status Card component that displays different status indicators with dynamic styling based on the current state. You'll learn how to create reusable Angular components that accept input properties and conditionally apply CSS classes to show various status types like success, warning, or error. The lesson covers core Angular concepts including component creation, property binding with @Input decorators, and conditional class binding using ngClass. You'll work with TypeScript interfaces to define status types, component templates for the HTML structure, and CSS styling to create visually distinct status indicators. By the end, you'll have a flexible status card that can be reused throughout an Angular application to communicate different states to users.
intro.usecase: Status cards are ubiquitous in modern web applications, appearing in dashboards to display system health, user activity, or performance metrics with color-coded indicators. They're commonly used in project management tools like Jira or Trello to show task status, in e-commerce admin panels to display order states, and in monitoring applications to indicate server uptime or alert conditions. Social media platforms use status cards to show user online/offline states, while enterprise software employs them for displaying approval workflows, document review states, or compliance statuses. As a developer, you'll frequently build these components to provide users with quick visual feedback about the current state of data or processes in your applications.

objectives: Construct an Angular component to display status information
Configure TypeScript properties to control status card appearance
Apply Angular data binding to connect component properties to the template
Implement conditional rendering to display different status states
Integrate CSS classes to style status cards based on their state
Bind click events to handle user interactions with status cards
Initialize component data to populate status card content

steps.title: Import Angular Component decorator
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the Component decorator that you'll need to create Angular components.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing a specific function from a library
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component decorator is imported from Angular core, making it available for creating components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with the import statement. Make sure you're importing Component from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: use the import statement to bring in Component from '@angular/core'. This follows the pattern: import { Component } from '@angular/core';

steps.title: Create the StatusCard component class
steps.instruction: Create a StatusCard component class and decorate it with the @Component decorator
steps.hint: Define a class named StatusCard and add the @Component decorator above it with basic metadata
steps.expectedOutcome: A StatusCard component class decorated with @Component that includes basic metadata
successCriteria: StatusCard class is created with @Component decorator including selector and template properties
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you have both the @Component decorator with metadata and the StatusCard class definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a class named StatusCard and decorate it with @Component that includes selector and template properties.

steps.title: Initialize status data properties
steps.instruction: Add three properties to the StatusCard component class: status (string), type (string), and icon (string) with initial values.
steps.hint: In Angular components, properties are declared as class members. You can assign default values directly to the properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StatusCard component class will have three properties: status, type, and icon, each with appropriate initial string values.
successCriteria: The component class contains status, type, and icon properties with string values assigned
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you have all three properties (status, type, icon) with initial string values assigned to each one.
steps.feedbackWrong: add three properties inside the StatusCard class: status, type, and icon. Each should be assigned an initial string value.

steps.title: Define the component template structure
steps.instruction: Replace the simple template div with a card container div that has the CSS class 'status-card' in the component decorator
steps.hint: Update the template property in the @Component decorator to use a div with class 'status-card' instead of the current simple div
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have a properly structured card container with CSS class for styling
successCriteria: Template contains a div with class 'status-card' as the main container
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the div has the class 'status-card' to properly style the card container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template needs a div element with class 'status-card' as the main container. Check your template property in the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Add status icon element
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add an icon element that displays the icon property using Angular interpolation
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display the icon property value in an icon element
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: displaying a property in an element {{userIcon}}
steps.expectedOutcome: An icon element displays the icon property value using Angular interpolation
successCriteria: Icon element is added to the template and uses interpolation to display the icon property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using interpolation {{ }} to display the icon property in an icon element.
steps.feedbackWrong: add an icon element (like <i> or <span>) that uses {{ }} interpolation to display the icon property value.

steps.title: Add status text display
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the comment to display the current status using string interpolation with the status property.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind the status property value in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: displaying a property value

Current theme: {{ theme }}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element displays the current status value using Angular interpolation syntax.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added that displays the status property using {{ status }} interpolation syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to use the {{ status }} syntax to display the status property value.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a paragraph element with {{ status }} to display the current status value.

steps.title: Apply conditional CSS classes
steps.instruction: Add ngClass directive to the status card div to dynamically apply CSS classes based on the type property
steps.hint: Use [ngClass] attribute binding to conditionally apply classes. You can bind to an object where keys are class names and values are boolean expressions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The status card div will have conditional CSS classes applied based on the component's type property
successCriteria: The div element uses [ngClass] directive to conditionally apply classes based on the type property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start with ngClass! Make sure you're binding to an object that uses the type property to determine which classes to apply.
steps.feedbackWrong: use [ngClass] with square brackets for property binding, and bind to an object where class names are keys and boolean expressions are values.

steps.title: Define component styles
steps.instruction: Add a styles array to the @Component decorator to define CSS for the status card and different status types
steps.hint: Add a 'styles' property to the @Component decorator with an array of CSS strings. Include styles for .status-card, .success, .error, and .warning classes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StatusCard component will have styles defined for the card container and different status types with appropriate colors and styling
successCriteria: A styles array is added to the @Component decorator with CSS rules for .status-card, .success, .error, and .warning classes
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your styles array includes CSS for .status-card as the base class and .success, .error, .warning for the different status types.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a 'styles' property to the @Component decorator with an array containing CSS strings for styling the status card.

steps.title: Add status update method
steps.instruction: Add a method named updateStatus inside the StatusCard class that takes two parameters (newStatus and newType) and updates the status and type properties accordingly
steps.hint: Define a method inside the class using the syntax methodName(parameters) { /* update properties */ }. Use this.propertyName to update the component properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StatusCard class will have an updateStatus method that can change the status and type properties when called
successCriteria: An updateStatus method is defined in the StatusCard class that accepts newStatus and newType parameters and updates the corresponding properties
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your method updates both the status and type properties using the parameters passed to it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateStatus method should be defined inside the StatusCard class and update both status and type properties using the method parameters.

steps.title: Add click handler for status toggle
steps.instruction: Add a (click) event binding on the status-card div that invokes updateStatus with two arguments: a new status string and a matching type string (for example literals or expressions that supply both values).
steps.hint: Event bindings use double quotes around the expression. Your method expects two parameters, so the template call needs two comma-separated arguments inside the parentheses.
steps.analogousExample:
// Passing arguments from the template into a class method
Save
steps.expectedOutcome: The status card div reacts to clicks by calling updateStatus with both a status value and a type value from the template.
successCriteria: The status-card div has a (click) binding whose expression calls updateStatus with two arguments
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add (click) on the div and ensure updateStatus is called with two values that match its parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use (click) on the status-card div and call updateStatus with two comma-separated arguments (for example two string literals) so the method receives both newStatus and newType.
